It is worth noting how broad Nash's work was. He did work in game theory, in topology,in geometry and in analysis. His work in game theory helped found modern game theory, and the development of the Nash embedding theorem was a major step in the study of Riemannian manifolds.Essentially he showed that if there's an abstract object (called a manifold) where you can put a very short-sighted ant on it, and the object always looks smooth and not too bumpy to the ant no matter where the object is, then you can actually fit that object into some space, possibly a space of high dimension. (This is only the rough flavor, I'm being deliberate vague on what one means because a lot of the terms are somewhat technical).
